bullets.title: GOOGL: Cloud +82% YoY, $514B backlog—but capex surge to $195-205B turns FCF negative
bullets.body: Alphabet Q2 revenue $119.8B beat consensus $117B; Cloud $24.77B crushed the $22.46B estimate with 82% YoY growth, $514B backlog, and 35.6% margins. FY26 capex raised $15B to $195-205B (2027 'to increase significantly'); Q2 FCF turned negative at -$5.9B for the first time. Gemini App at 950M MAU, AI Mode at 1B+ MAU. TPU sales recognized as material GCP revenue. Street reactions: JPM reiterates OW, cuts PT to $420; MS cuts PT to $400 (OW); Citi reiterates Buy, $447; RJ lowers PT to $400 (Strong Buy); UBS cuts PT to $379, Neutral; Mizuho raises cloud ests, maintains $460 PT; Piper cuts PT to $395. Consensus: buy-on-pullback with FCF/capex ROI as key debate.

bullets.title: TSLA: Revenue beats, margins crush—$0.33 EPS vs $0.55 est; FCF -$1.1B; enters bear market
bullets.body: Tesla Q2 revenue $28.24B beat estimates of $26.3B (+26% YoY); adjusted EPS $0.33 missed $0.55 consensus. Gross margin 16.8% vs 19.4-19.5% expected; auto gross margin ex-credits only 16.3%. CapEx $5.8B drove FCF to -$1.1B, first negative in 2+ years. Optimus SOP targeted late 2026; Cybercab in production in 7 cities with 380K+ unsupervised miles; FSD attach rate 55%. CFO guides capex growth for 2-3 more years. Morgan Stanley cuts PT to $400; Mizuho $450; Canaccord $410. Stock down 7%+ pre-market, entering 20%-bear-market territory.

bullets.title: NOW: Q2 strong beat-and-raise; AI ACV crosses $1B; +5% pre-market
bullets.body: ServiceNow F2Q subscription revenue +23% CC (150bps beat); cRPO +21.5% CC (200bps beat); operating margin 29.4% (+300bps). AI ACV surpassed $1B with net-new ACV +40% Q/Q; agentic AI buyers up 45% YoY. FY26 subscription revenue raised to ~$15.77B (+21% CC). Q3 subscription guide slightly below consensus due to Federal pull-forward. Wolfe raises PT to $140; JPM raises to $150 (OW); Mizuho reiterates $140; UBS cuts PT to $110 (Neutral, 'skinny beat'). Stock +5% pre-market.

bullets.title: TXN: Beat-and-raise; data center doubled YoY; industrial +30%; UBS raises PT to $380
bullets.body: Texas Instruments Q2 revenue $5.46B beat consensus $5.24B; EPS $2.14 vs $1.93; FCF $2.74B well above consensus. Q3 guided $5.90B midpoint (+8% QoQ, far above seasonal); EPS $2.41. Data center revenue doubled YoY and now ~13% of sales; automotive mid-teens YoY on China EV strength; industrial +30% YoY. Pricing increases in 2H26, more impact 4Q26. UBS raises PT to $380 (Buy); Wolfe reiterates OW, $360; Citi $345 (Buy, top analog pick); KeyBanc raises PT to $400.

bullets.title: AT&T: Strong 2Q; fiber at multi-year highs; buyback to $10B; multiple upgrades
bullets.body: AT&T Q2 EBITDA +5.2% YoY; postpaid phone adds 432K (beat); fiber adds 367K (multi-year high); FWA +279K; churn improved to 0.86%. Accelerating buyback to $10B in FY26 (from $8B); convergence rate 42.5%. Morgan Stanley raises PT to $27, OW; Citi Buy $28; UBS upgrades to Buy; JPM raises PT to $33 (Dec-27); Wolfe upgrades to Outperform, $29. Multiple bullish catalysts: Lumen accretion, cost takeout, Starlink risk overstated.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Q2 in-line; Peacock profitable; wireless +448K; buyback paused pre-separation
bullets.body: Comcast Q2 revenue $29.94B beat $29.24B consensus; FCF $4.60B well above consensus $3.6-3.7B; EPS $1.04 beat $0.97. Wireless net adds 448K beat 395K consensus; Peacock turned profitable at $189M EBITDA, subs 48M. HSD broadband losses -167K slightly worse than expected; Theme Parks soft. Company paused buybacks ahead of planned business separation. Citi maintains Buy, $32 PT; UBS Neutral; KeyBanc Sector Weight.

bullets.title: GEV: Raised guidance, 20GW new contracts; MS raises PT to $1,350—9% selloff 'overdone'
bullets.body: GE Vernova Q2 data-center orders $5B (2x FY25); signed 20GW of new gas turbine contracts vs 10-15GW guidance; raising capacity to 30GW by 2030 from 24GW prior. Revenue guidance raised $1B; FCF doubled. MS raises PT to $1,350 (from $1,250), OW—calls yesterday's 9% decline an overreaction. TD Cowen raises to $1,235; RBC $1,225. Stock sold off on end-of-decade oversupply fears but JPM/MS view those concerns as overstated given 2031 capacity already 50% pre-sold.

bullets.title: AMD + Anthropic: $5B investment, 2GW MI450 deployment—major signal for 2027 data center GPU revenue
bullets.body: AMD and Anthropic announced a strategic expansion: up to 2GW Instinct MI450 GPU deployment by Anthropic and a $5B equity investment from AMD in Anthropic. UBS frames deal as conviction signal for AMD's 2027 data center GPU revenue step-up. ROCm development acceleration via Claude Code also highlighted, with AMD using Anthropic to help close the CUDA gap.

bullets.title: INTC + AMD: Long-term CPU agreements with Chinese data center customers; prices up 40%+ YTD
bullets.body: Reuters reports Intel and AMD signing multi-year (1-2+ year) purchase commitments with major Chinese server customers for data-center CPUs. CPU product prices in China up 40%+ since start of year, with some month-on-month increases exceeding 10%. Intel also exploring an operating partnership for its delayed $28B Ohio fab with SK Hynix as a candidate. INTC +1% pre-market.

bullets.title: PLTR: Citi raises estimates on commercial reacceleration; cuts PT to $200 on multiple compression
bullets.body: Citi expects Palantir US Commercial to rebound in Q2 with RDV net adds returning to $800-900M range (+record territory). Intra-Q checks positive; large insurance win in Mexico and deepening NVDA sovereign product relationship. FY27 topline at 53% YoY growth (~8pts above consensus). PT cut to $200 (from higher) due to software multiple compression across the industry, but rating maintained as Buy.

bullets.title: LVS: Q2 EBITDA misses in both Macau and Singapore; PT cuts; $6B buyback authorized
bullets.body: Las Vegas Sands Q2 Macau EBITDA $513-517M vs Street $556-562M; Singapore EBITDA $652M vs ~$722-725M estimate. World Cup impacted VIP in both markets; Macau mass table hold hit record low. Board authorized new $6B buyback (22% of market cap). JPM cuts PT to $60 (OW); Mizuho cuts PT to $61; StreetAccount notes Street sees limited downside given Marina Bay Sands undervaluation.

bullets.title: TMUS: Q2 EBITDA beat, FCF raised to $18.4-18.8B; Wolfe upgrades with $255 PT
bullets.body: T-Mobile Q2 core adj. EBITDA $9.54B beat consensus $9.4B; FCF $4.8B beat; postpaid account adds 277K beat. FY26 FCF guidance raised $200M to $18.4-18.8B; EBITDA guidance maintained $37.1-37.5B. Postpaid churn rose 7bps to 0.99%. UBS maintains Buy ($225); Wolfe upgrades to Outperform ($255, 33% upside); KeyBanc Overweight $260. Slight negative: service revenue $18.98B marginally missed consensus.

bullets.title: NOK: AI & Cloud orders €2.8B in Q2—more than 2x Q1; Morgan Stanley upgrades to OW
bullets.body: Nokia Q2 AI & Cloud order intake €2.8B vs €1B in Q1 (+105% revenue YoY); now 9% of group sales. Q2 EBIT beat consensus by 15%. FY26 comparable operating profit expected 'somewhat above midpoint' of €2.1-2.6B guidance. Supply constraints (not demand) are gating factor. NOK to acquire portion of NXP Arizona fab for InP optical production, converting to 300mm by Q1 2029. Morgan Stanley upgrades to OW with €14 PT.

bullets.title: LYV: BTIG initiates Buy with $215 PT (21% upside)
bullets.body: BTIG analyst Tyler DiMatteo initiated coverage of Live Nation Entertainment with Buy rating and $215 price target, implying 21% upside from $177.92. FactSet consensus target is $192.61.

bullets.title: HUBS: Reseller survey turns more pessimistic; Citi cautious on GTM execution
bullets.body: Citi reseller survey shows HubSpot 2Q quota performance deteriorated: resellers missed quotas by 180bps in Q2 vs surpassing by 60bps in Q1. NTM growth expectations cut 220bps to +1.6% YoY. Citi flagged meaningful GTM execution risk; expects modest Q2 beat but unlikely FY26 guidance raise. PT moved to $217.

bullets.title: SHOP: Citi raises PT to $150; expects 2Q sales growth ~29% YoY (~100bps above Street)
bullets.body: Citi expects Shopify to deliver Q2 sales growth of 29% YoY, about 100bps above Street, with room for low-thirties. Q3 guidance also expected above Street despite tougher comps. Citi raises SHOP PT to $150 based on 48.5x FY28 EV/FCF, noting bifurcated software environment is favoring e-commerce and B2C.

bullets.title: MU: YMTC reportedly surpasses Micron in NAND market share; NAND still in short supply
bullets.body: Per third-party data cited on X, YMTC has surpassed Micron and SanDisk in NAND market share and is within 0.4pp of Kioxia. Separately, Elon Musk disclosed Micron gave Tesla a 'significant allocation' of memory chips. A social media post warning about YMTC was clarified as not a sell signal, with the author noting NAND remains in short supply.

bullets.title: MSFT: KeyBanc bullish ahead of Q4; eyes path to mid-40s Azure growth; $600 PT
bullets.body: KeyBanc maintains OW on MSFT ahead of Q4 results, with $600 PT. 57% of 21 partners surveyed are ahead of plan. Azure needs to reach 45%+ growth to drive stock rally vs consensus 41%. MSFT estimated ~$250B FY27 capex (vs $232B consensus). Copilot feedback improving. JPM Tech Sketch flags MSFT as having worst sentiment among Mag 7, lacking tangible AI progress (no proprietary LLM, chip, or Copilot wins) and sees equity raise possibility as 'non-zero'.

bullets.title: LITE: Pre-market +1.2%; disproportionate beneficiary of GOOGL TPU/capex ramp
bullets.body: Lumentum shares rose 1.2% in pre-market on Google capex surge. Multiple sources note LITE disproportionately benefits from Google's TPU build-out and capex expansion. BTIG analyst Kevin Garrigan separately noted CPO is entering volume manufacturing per NVDA. Lumentum CEO also spoke at RAISE Summit highlighting AI.

bullets.title: LLY: TRIUMPH-2 and -3 phase 3 data strengthen retatrutide best-in-class case; Citi Buy, $1,600 PT
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on Eli Lilly at $1,600 PT (38% total return). TRIUMPH-2 showed 8.7-16.8% placebo-adjusted weight loss in T2D/obesity patients; TRIUMPH-3 showed 18.4-19.4% weight loss in severe obesity with CVD. Five positive Phase 3 studies support obesity, knee osteoarthritis, and sleep apnea indications. FDA submission planned 1Q27; Bloomberg consensus 2035 peak sales $12.3B.
